title: The screening's capacity under production limits (audit #53 part 1; the founder's rulings of 2026-10-20, decisions 13 to 16, of 2026-10-21, Q1 (a), Q7 and Q8, and of 2026-10-23, S4's median of three and time advisory)
assertion: The production images at production's task sizes, the screening consumer among them (WORKER_JOBS=screening at 2 vCPU and 4 GiB, three threads, on its own login) beside a platform that prices none, Postgres at db.t4g.medium's 2 vCPU with gp3's baseline and a 2 ms round trip, on GitHub's free 4-CPU runner in its shared layout (Postgres, the harness and Chromium on 0-1, the consumer on 2-3, the web and the platform on 3; on eight CPUs or more each service on CPUs of its own, derived the same way from environments.ts's sizes, the report naming which ran), the SYNTHETIC scale release (2.2 million records): the practice and worst 50,000-row uploads alone and three at once (cold, the worst ones distinct, each upload a prospect of its own; the three worst at once, S4, run three times, S4#1 to S4#3, each cold with the same uploads from prospects of their own) with a small one sent once the large uploads' jobs are queued; fails on an OOM kill (Postgres's included), a restart, anonymous memory above 90% of a limit (the consumer's included), a limit or cold start not applied, the consumer measured at another size than declared or its threads not pricing at once (a free thread takes the next normal job at once: each send to a screening queue wakes the consumer's workers through LISTEN/NOTIFY and each run's end wakes them again, pg-boss's 2-s poll kept as the fallback), a runner too small (fewer than 4 CPUs, each need named), a layout other than the one the harness gives the runner, a container or the harness off its layout's CPUs, a wrong, unfinished or stalled result, a result page that does not open (its first page of groups or its last), a small upload not queued behind the large ones, the platform pricing a screening, a process-runtime layout missing what the images hold (PROCESS_IMAGES_INCOMPLETE), an upload in the waiting tier, the consumer's time to email not logged or out of its bounds (never above the time from the harness's click to its own line, never more than 2 s below the harness's, the web's receipt stamped by its proxy before the body is read), a request that left for the static origin, an oracle mismatch or an oracle short of an upload's Medicare rows (S1-1, S2-1 and S3-1 against the read and adapter frozen at 3c1b289, and S1-2, a ZIP the release splits across localities sent with its ZIP+4, against the whole-release oracle), or a run of fewer than S1 to S5 with S4's three runs, every one of these checks holding in each of S4's runs; time judged: any upload above 48 s on the runner (60 s scaled by the runner-to-Fargate factor once staging measures it), S4's on its middle run alone (its runs ordered by their worst large upload, all four of the middle run's uploads judged; the founder's ruling of 2026-10-23, kept in both time modes), fails a binding run (a release's) and is a warning in an advisory one (every other run's: a pull request's job and gate pass on time warnings alone and fail on any other check; the founder's third ruling of 2026-10-23, time advisory), and a worst judged time above 44 s goes to the founder as a sizing question, shown on the pull request's checks as a warning; required on every pull request through a gate that runs even after a cancel and measures when a path of the derived watched list changed (the import closure of the screening's entry points and the files no import reaches, held equal to what watched.ts derives); the release loader analyzes and freezes rule_record after a load, and the keyed read probes the index per key (operator_screening_run_keys estimated at one row)
noFileReason: The capacity test builds its SYNTHETIC scale release and uploads outside the repository when it runs; no file is committed.
